record.paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
record.original_question: For a normal projected entangled pair state (PEPS) with bond dimension D, what is the exact best possible upper bound, in terms of D alone, for its injectivity index?

evidence.quote: Question 4 Which is the optimal upper bound for the injectivity index of a normal PEPS in terms of its bond dimension?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $D \geq 2$ be an integer (the bond dimension) and let $d \geq 1$ be a physical dimension. A PEPS tensor on a square lattice is a tensor $A \in \mathbb{C}^{d} \otimes (\mathbb{C}^{D})^{\otimes 4}$ with one physical index of dimension $d$ and four virtual indices of dimension $D$ (one per lattice direction). For a finite simply connected region $R$ of the square lattice, the associated linear map
$$\Gamma_R : (\mathbb{C}^{D})^{\otimes \partial R} \longrightarrow (\mathbb{C}^{d})^{\otimes |R|}$$
is obtained by placing a copy of $A$ at every site of $R$, contracting all virtual indices internal to $R$, and leaving the virtual indices on the boundary $\partial R$ open.

A PEPS tensor $A$ is called injective on the region $R$ if $\Gamma_R$ is an injective linear map. The PEPS is called normal if there exists some finite region $R_0$ on which $\Gamma_{R_0}$ is injective; equivalently, normality means injectivity is reached on some sufficiently large patch. The injectivity index of a normal PEPS is defined as the smallest integer $L = L(A)$ such that $\Gamma_R$ is injective for every $L \times L$ square region $R$ (or, equivalently, for every region containing an $L \times L$ square).

Question. Determine the optimal (i.e. smallest) function $f : \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 2} \to \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$ depending only on the bond dimension $D$ such that for every normal PEPS tensor $A$ with bond dimension $D$, the injectivity index satisfies
$$L(A) \leq f(D),$$
and such that this bound is attained by some normal PEPS with bond dimension $D$. In other words, give the exact best possible upper bound, expressed solely in terms of $D$, on the injectivity index of a normal PEPS of bond dimension $D$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on PEPS (e.g. SciPost Phys. 9, 042 (2020); arXiv:1706.07329; arXiv:2509.19963) discusses injectivity and provides bounds in various refined or generalized settings, but no source identifies the exact optimal upper bound on the injectivity index of a normal PEPS purely in terms of the bond dimension D. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Tensor network representations from the geometry of entangled states (SciPost)
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds on the required bond dimensions for tensor network classes including PEPS and generalized injective PEPS are proved.
status_evidence.claim: Provides upper/lower bounds on bond dimensions for injective PEPS but does not pin down the optimal injectivity index in terms of D.

status_evidence.title: A generalization of the injectivity condition for PEPS
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces semi-injective PEPS and discusses injectivity conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Generalizes injectivity but does not determine the optimal bound on the injectivity index.

status_evidence.title: Computational complexity of injective PEPS
status_evidence.snippet: Quantifies injectivity via condition number parameter delta, studies computational thresholds.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on injective PEPS that does not resolve the optimal injectivity-index bound.
